title: Decimal Division Word Problems: Decimal Group Sizes
intro: Explain division by a decimal using a clearly labeled group size.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Show full and partial groups in the original units. Then scale both numbers together to make the division easier.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Two groups use 0.9 + 0.9 = 1.8 units. The remaining 0.45 is half of 0.9, so it contributes another half-group. The answer is 2.5 groups. The empty dashed half shows the size of a complete third group; it is not part of the given total.

Ask your student

Why must both numbers change by the same factor?

If your student needs help

If the student changes only the divisor, compare the new model with the original total.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set includes two divisors below one and two above one. Predict whether the quotient will be numerically larger or smaller than the dividend before calculating. This prediction compares the quotient with the dividend; it does not say whether the quotient itself is above or below one.
